study.name: Interview
study.about: Video người nói nền tối, từ khóa xanh chanh cỡ lớn, chữ trắng xếp lệch và đồ họa nhấn theo lời nói.
study.visualRules: Keep the supplied speaker footage. Recreate the Interview reference with compact mixed-size typography near the chest: one lime #D7FF55 hero keyword in heavy Inter Tight, roughly 2.5 times the size of nearby small off-white support clauses. Keep the phrases centered and tightly grouped, with supporting words above, beside, or below the hero; do not stack every word at headline size. Reveal each spoken phrase in place as it is said, then replace the group at the next idea. Use a red diagonal strike with thin vertical scanlines for a spoken failure or negation; a rough olive brush highlight for a positive key idea; and REC corners only when recording or camera anxiety is actually discussed. Preserve the source skin tone and keep text off the face. Do not copy the reference video speech or camera props into unrelated footage.
study.motionRules: Change text and overlays at spoken idea boundaries. Sampled frames show words being added and layouts being replaced, but do not establish entrance direction, easing, animation duration, or continuous zoom. Keep graphic positions steady while held. Use cuts as a conservative render choice where a transition is required.
study.soundRules: Sync visuals to the supplied speech. Music, level, tempo, and sound effects are unverified; add no signature whoosh, pop, beep, or glitch sound based on the images alone.
study.limitations: Inter Tight is the closest listed match to the observed heavy geometric sans; the exact font is unknown. Playfair Display is the closest listed option for the brief italic serif in the final value bar. One-second frame samples do not establish exact cut points, motion, zoom, or transition type. The sampled study does not establish audio treatment.
study.editRules: Open on a complete thought spoken in the new video. Break important clauses into small white supporting words and one larger lime keyword. Keep the group in a shared safe rectangle: the first support row leans left, the hero row stays centered, and the last support row leans right without clipping. Reveal semantic runs at their spoken times, hold earlier runs in place, and replace the group when the idea changes. Use a brush, strike with scanlines, or REC frame only when the new speech supports that motif. Keep quieter explanation passages as subtitles; do not transplant the reference speaker wording, camera props, or service labels into unrelated content.
study.assetRules: Use the supplied speaker footage and preserve skin tone. Add reference motifs only when the new speech and footage support them: red strike and scanlines for a negative claim, rough olive brush for a strong positive idea, REC corners for recording anxiety, and list cards only for an actual spoken list. Do not invent a camera, microphone, avatar, or reference-video text over unrelated footage. If supporting assets are unavailable, keep compact white and lime typography over the speaker.
recipeChecks: Small off-white support clauses frame a substantially larger lime keyword in compact rows near the speaker chest.
Spoken runs appear one by one while earlier runs hold position; phrases change at idea boundaries.
A red strike and fine scanlines appear for spoken failure or negation, an olive brush mark for a selected affirmative idea, and REC corners only when the speech concerns recording.
Reference-only words, props, cards and camera shots are not inserted when the new speech or footage does not support them.
No sound effect or exact easing is assumed from sampled reference frames.
visualMotifs: On ‘prospects’ around 0–1 s, place a large lime ‘Prospects’ across the speaker’s chest while smaller white words accumulate around it; the exact reveal motion is unknown.
On ‘your content is failing’ around 3–4 s, retain the chest-level lime ‘Content’, add white ‘is failing’, cross ‘Content’ with a red diagonal stroke, and cover the frame with fine vertical stripes.
On ‘You know content matters’ around 5 s, shift large white and lime text to the top of the frame and let the speaker’s head occlude part of ‘content’.
On ‘being on camera stresses you out’ around 6–7 s, show the speaker within a cream ring beside foreground camera equipment, with the white and lime phrase above; the ring’s animation is unverified.

On ‘unsure of what to say’ through ‘real revenue’ around 9–14 s, hold white REC corners over the speaker, replace the large lime ‘You record’ with a dark red ‘what to say?’ bar, then add a second revenue question bar below.

On ‘We plan, shoot, script, edit, and post’ around 17–20 s, show PLAN at lower left, expand to a three-card PLAN/SHOOT/SCRIPT row, then replace it with larger EDIT/POST cards; the cards’ entrance motion is unknown.
